stories.title: First Appearance in Shegaon and Recognition at Devidas's Feast

boundary_evidence.reason: The narrator turns to the great man himself and to his coming to Shegaon (ovi 70-83); ovi 83-84 then tie the feast to that time, so one story begins here.
He comes to Shegaon in his prime: the arrival that the encounter follows.
After the teaching and the men's readiness to surrender, Gajanan runs off like the wind, closing the encounter.

scenes.brief: Opening, two shots. Narrated: his place and caste cannot be traced (70-73). On screen: only the year 1878 as a caption. Shot 1: historical Shegaon (58-60). Shot 2: the young Gajanan seen there. No birthplace, childhood, parents or journey is shown.

Devidas prepares his son's Ritushanti feast; outside, the almost bare stranger (worn old bandi, digambar) picks leftover rice grains from the leaf plates; narrator gives the teaching 'food is Brahman' (94-96).
Bankatlal and Damodarpant see him, debate whether he is mad or profoundly wise, and resolve to test his conduct rather than dismiss him.
Bankatlal humbly asks why he searches the plates; no answer, only a steady look at both; radiant, absorbed in inner bliss; the two visitors bow to him in silence (ovi 112).

After a request whose speaker is unnamed, Devidas sets a plate of rich cooked dishes before Gajanan; he mixes all the dishes together and eats without liking or disliking any taste (118); narrator's two comparisons (116-117).

Bankatlal tells Damodarpant that calling him mad was a mistake; like Arjuna for Subhadra, Gajanan seeks liberation; no further test is needed. Ovi 122 praises Shegaon and Hari's gift of desirelessness; speaker unclear.
At noon the gourd is empty; Damodarpant offers water, Gajanan laughingly explains practical conduct, and Damodarpant joyfully enters Devidas's house to fetch water in a gadva.
Gajanan drinks at the cattle trough beside the well; Damodarpant returns with cool, vetiver-scented water and protests that the muddy water is fit only for animals.
Gajanan declares that water in any form and the drinker are one in Brahman (138-142), with room for his words; the men are ready to fall at his feet (143); he runs off like the wind (144).

unfilmed_ranges.reason: Invocations to deities and saints, with the author's humility and prayer for guidance in composing the work.
The author exhorts listeners and praises saints; these verses narrate no story event.
Lists of earlier saints, earlier books and the author's plan explain the lineage and purpose of this biography.
Shegaon, Patil's request and the praise of the true saint set the scene; one view of Shegaon is drawn from 58-60 as context.
The narrator contrasts unobservant passers-by with the discerning gem-picker; this is reflective narration, not required action.
The next-chapter announcement and the author's prayerful dedication close the chapter.

direction_notes: Opening: exactly two shots. The year 1878 appears only as an on-screen caption (the owner's instruction; the Granth says 'within Shaka 1800s'); no day or month; do not invent a birthplace, childhood, parents or a journey into Shegaon; no Sajjangad, Samarth Ramdas or Nath-yogi material in the narration or the pictures.
Dress: a worn old bandi (88) and otherwise almost bare (digambar, 92), throughout; a self-made UNFIRED clay chilim (90) and a gourd (89). The sunrise comparison (91) is not a time-of-day instruction.
Show the 'food is Brahman' explanation (94-96) with the grain-picking action (93-94).
The visitors bow to him in silence at 112 (no spoken words); at 143 the men are only READY to fall at his feet.
Show the mixing of the dishes before he eats (118); keep both narrator comparisons (116-117).

Damodarpant (not Bankatlal) fetches the water: he enters Devidas's house (133) and returns with the gadva (135). The trough is beside the well; he belches with satisfaction (134-135); he is not stated to drink the water Damodarpant brings.
Keep his teaching complete (138-142) and do not shorten it to fit a six-second shot; at 144 he runs with NO destination.
Ovis 103-104, 113 and 122-124 keep their unclear speaker: do not give those words to a named person.
